tokens.text: // saxpy trio: streaming update, reversed gather, dot-product reduction.
// plus a branch-heavy helper so the CFG view shows two functions.
// loop #0 - elementwise stream: iterations are independent
// loop #1 - reversed gather: carries a RAW dependence

functions.name: main
functions.text:
;; helix IR - pre-SSA (print_ir ssa=false)
fn main() -> () {
bb0:                                            ; preds: []
    n   = const 33554432         ; i64
    x   = alloc_array [f64] n
    y   = alloc_array [f64] n
    h   = sdiv n, 2              ; i64
    dot = const 0.0              ; f64
    i   = const 0                ; i64
    jump bb1

bb1:                                            ; preds: bb0 bb3 | loop#0 header (depth 1)
    c0 = icmp ult i, n
    br c0, bb2, bb4

bb2:                                            ; loop#0 body
    t0 = fmul 2.5, load x[i]
    t1 = load y[i]
    t2 = fadd t0, t1
    store y[i], t2
    jump bb3

bb3:                                            ; loop#0 latch
    i = add i, 1
    jump bb1

bb4:                                            ; preds: bb1 | loop#1 preheader
    j = const 0
    jump bb5

bb5:                                            ; preds: bb4 bb7 | loop#1 header (depth 1)
    c1 = icmp ult j, h
    br c1, bb6, bb8

bb6:                                            ; loop#1 body
    t3 = sub n, j
    t4 = sub t3, 1
    t5 = load y[t4]
    store y[j], t5
    jump bb7

bb7:                                            ; loop#1 latch
    j = add j, 1
    jump bb5

bb8:                                            ; preds: bb5 | loop#2 preheader
    dot = const 0.0
    k   = const 0
    jump bb9

bb9:                                            ; preds: bb8 bb11 | loop#2 header (depth 1)
    c2 = icmp ult k, n
    br c2, bb10, bb12

bb10:                                           ; loop#2 body
    t6  = load x[k]
    t7  = load y[k]
    t8  = fmul t6, t7
    t9  = fadd dot, t8
    dot = t9
    jump bb11

bb11:                                           ; loop#2 latch
    k = add k, 1
    jump bb9

bb12:                                           ; preds: bb9 | exit
    call print(dot)
    ret ()}

;; helix IR - pre-SSA (print_ir ssa=false)
fn clampidx(i: i64, n: i64) -> i64 {
bb0:                                            ; preds: []
    c0 = icmp slt i, 0
    br c0, bb1, bb2

bb1:                                            ; preds: bb0
    ret 0

bb2:                                            ; preds: bb0
    c1 = icmp sge i, n
    br c1, bb3, bb4

bb3:                                            ; preds: bb2
    t0 = sub n, 1
    ret t0

bb4:                                            ; preds: bb2
    ret i
}

functions.text:
;; helix IR - after SSA construction (print_ir ssa=true)
fn main() -> () {
bb0:                                            ; preds: []
    n.0   = const 33554432       ; i64
    x.0   = alloc_array [f64] n.0
    y.0   = alloc_array [f64] n.0
    h.0   = sdiv n.0, 2          ; i64
    dot.0 = const 0.0            ; f64
    i.0   = const 0              ; i64
    jump bb1(i.0)

bb1:                                            ; preds: bb0 bb3 | loop#0 header (depth 1)
    i.1 = phi(i.0 [bb0], i.2 [bb3])          ; iv: i in [0, n.0)
    c0  = icmp ult i.1, n.0
    br c0, bb2, bb4

bb2:                                            ; loop#0 body
    t0.1 = fmul 2.5, load x.0[i.1]
    t1.1 = load y.0[i.1]
    t2.1 = fadd t0.1, t1.1
    store y.0[i.1], t2.1
    jump bb3

bb3:                                            ; loop#0 latch
    i.2 = add i.1, 1
    jump bb1

bb4:                                            ; preds: bb1 | loop#1 preheader
    j.0 = const 0
    jump bb5

bb5:                                            ; preds: bb4 bb7 | loop#1 header (depth 1)
    j.1 = phi(j.0 [bb4], j.2 [bb7])          ; iv: j in [0, h.0)
    c1  = icmp ult j.1, h.0
    br c1, bb6, bb8

bb6:                                            ; loop#1 body
    t3.1 = sub n.0, j.1
    t4.1 = sub t3.1, 1
    t5.1 = load y.0[t4.1]
    store y.0[j.1], t5.1
    jump bb7

bb7:                                            ; loop#1 latch
    j.2 = add j.1, 1
    jump bb5

bb8:                                            ; preds: bb5 | loop#2 preheader
    dot.1 = const 0.0
    k.0   = const 0
    jump bb9

bb9:                                            ; preds: bb8 bb11 | loop#2 header (depth 1)
    k.1   = phi(k.0 [bb8], k.2 [bb11])       ; iv: k in [0, n.0)
    dot.3 = phi(dot.1 [bb8], dot.2 [bb11])   ; reduction cell: dot
    c2    = icmp ult k.1, n.0
    br c2, bb10, bb12

bb10:                                           ; loop#2 body
    t6.1  = load x.0[k.1]
    t7.1  = load y.0[k.1]
    t8.1  = fmul t6.1, t7.1
    dot.2 = fadd dot.3, t8.1
    jump bb11

bb11:                                           ; loop#2 latch
    k.2 = add k.1, 1
    jump bb9

bb12:                                           ; preds: bb9 | exit
    call print(dot.3)
    ret ()}

functions.name: clampidx
functions.text:
;; helix IR - after SSA construction (print_ir ssa=true)
fn clampidx(i.0: i64, n.0: i64) -> i64 {
bb0:                                            ; preds: []
    c0 = icmp slt i.0, 0
    br c0, bb1, bb2

bb1:                                            ; preds: bb0
    ret 0

bb2:                                            ; preds: bb0
    c1 = icmp sge i.0, n.0
    br c1, bb3, bb4

bb3:                                            ; preds: bb2
    t0.1 = sub n.0, 1
    ret t0.1

bb4:                                            ; preds: bb2
    ret i.0
}

loops.reason: no loop-carried dependences: each iteration touches a distinct y[i]
loops.explain: Every store targets y[i] and every load reads x[i] or y[i] at the same subscript i. The dependence graph has no cycles, so iterations may execute in any order - the runtime strips the loop across 16 threads.

raw.explain: iteration j reads y[n-j-1], written by iteration j-1 when n-j-1 equals j-1 at the crossing point; dependence distance is 1, so no reordering is legal.

loops.reason: loop-carried RAW dependence at distance 1 on y: y[j] reads y[n - j - 1] written one iteration earlier
loops.explain: The reversed gather walks the same array forwards and backwards. Near the midpoint the read subscript aliases the previous iteration's write, producing a distance-1 RAW chain that forces fully sequential execution.

loops.reason: +-reduction into dot: sum is re-associated under the f64 fast-math contract
loops.explain: dot accumulates a sum of products. Each thread keeps a private accumulator and the partial sums are combined at the loop exit; results are deterministic up to f64 addition re-association.
